subject: Private control plane identity connector design + fallback options
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: security@datahub.com, okta-sales@okta.com
Date: Thu, 9 May 2024 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private control plane identity connector design + fallback options

Hi team,

Following up from yesterday's sync with DataHub — they want a design that supports their on-prem IdP (SAML), SCIM-based provisioning into the private control plane, and a clear fallback so that if SCIM provisioning or assertion-mapped roles fail we still keep minimal admin access to the control plane.

I attached an initial SCIM group mapping (scim_group_map_v1.csv) and a quick authn proxy flow (saml_authn_proxy_flow.png). High-level asks:
- Confirm the recommended role mapping (SCIM groups -> Redwood roles) and whether we need an additional tenant-level denylist for sensitive roles.
- Decide where the AuthN proxy runs in the VPC: runner on customer side (recommended) vs a hosted proxy with secure peering.
- Define a fallback admin path (short-lived service account vs hosted emergency access) and audit expectations.

Can Marcus and Laura review the mappings and the playbook (delegated-admin-playbook.docx) and call out any policy or ops blockers before I share the design with DataHub next week?

Best,
Rachel
Rachel Kim
Senior Security PM, Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: rachel_kim@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 9 May 2024 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private control plane identity connector design + fallback options

Thanks Rachel — reviewed the attachments. Quick notes:

1) SCIM mapping
- scim_group_map_v1.csv looks fine as a starting point. Recommend mapping the customer 'infra-admins' group to Redwood 'priv-admin' and enforce a second factor check for any role that can modify billing/SLA settings.
- Add an explicit 'audit-only' group mapping for groups that get read-only access to logs.

2) AuthN proxy placement
- Strong preference: run the AuthN proxy as a customer-owned container in their VPC (sidecar or small service) so assertions never leave the tenant network. We can support a hosted proxy only if mutual TLS + IP whitelisting is enforced and we sign an MOA.

3) Fallback admin path
- Option A (preferred): short-lived service account generated by the private control plane that requires: a documented justification ticket + approval from 2 internal approvers. Tokens expire at 1h. All actions are logged to the customer's audit bucket.
- Option B: hosted emergency admin that we grant via support for escalations — higher risk and needs contract-level attestations.

4) SCIM sync behavior
- Must surface errors and deltas to both the customer and us. Retry policy: exponential backoff + alerting after 3 consecutive fails.

I'll annotate scim_group_map_v1.csv with my comments and upload. If we go with the short-lived service account we should wire it into our existing KMS workflow and make the creation auditable via the control plane trace.

—Marcus
Principal Infra Engineer
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: rachel_kim@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, security@datahub.com
Date: Fri, 10 May 2024 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private control plane identity connector design + fallback options

Nice write-up. A couple of compliance/ops questions from my side:

- Delegated admin: if we allow delegated admin in the customer's tenant, what is our incident process if a delegated admin misconfigures a routing policy? Do we block changes for 30m after a high-risk change? Do we require canary changes?
- Audit logs retention: DataHub requested 18 months; our baseline is 12 months on hosted, 24 months configurable for Dedicated. We should document costs and the retention toggle in the playbook.
- Legal: DataHub asked for explicit SAML assertion retention rules (they do not want assertions stored). We should ensure our proxy does not persist assertions and that any diagnostic logs are scrubbed.

Also, can we make the fallback path explicit in the runbook with the required approvals and a contact tree? I started a draft in the playbook with a sample change request form.

Laura
Director, Product Ops
From: Okta Team <okta-sales@okta.com>

Subject: Re: Private control plane identity connector design + fallback options

Hi Rachel/Marcus —

Thanks for looping us in. A few constraints from the IdP side:
- Okta's SCIM push is rate-limited at the org level; large directory syncs should be batched. Recommend implementing incremental SCIM delta syncs and a full reconciliation once daily.
- SAML assertions: our best practice is to include roles in the assertion as group claims, but customers can choose to send group-membership via SCIM instead.
- We can support an SP-initiated flow via the proxy; the proxy should validate signature timestamps and reject replayed assertions.

We have a lightweight SCIM connector template we can share (small code sample + Helm chart). Attaching internal doc/sample to the Drive link you provided.

—Okta Solutions Engineering
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: rachel_kim@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: security@datahub.com
Date: Wed, 15 May 2024 09:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private control plane identity connector design + fallback options

Circling back after internal runbook review. A couple of operational items to add to the checklist:

- Health endpoints: the AuthN proxy must expose a /health and /metrics endpoint that our ops can scrape over the secured peering connection. If running customer-side, we need the customer to enable VPC Peering and provide an endpoint ACL.
- Key rotation: if we provide a short-lived service account, rotation must be automated and logged to the customer's S3 bucket. We should publish a key-rotation cadence (default 1 day) and a renewal API.
- Emergency path test: run quarterly disaster recovery drills that validate fallback admin creation and revocation. Document the drill steps in delegated-admin-playbook.docx.

Action: I'll add a small section to the playbook with the health-check and rotation API contract.

Grace
Infrastructure Reliability Manager

Thanks all — good feedback. Summary / next steps before I share with DataHub on Friday:

1) SCIM mapping: Marcus will finalize scim_group_map_v1.csv with the 'priv-admin' and 'audit-only' entries.
2) AuthN proxy: recommend customer-run proxy in VPC; Okta to provide SCIM connector template — Rachel to capture networking ACL requirements.
3) Fallback admin: adopt Option A (short-lived service account) with 1-hour TTL and two-approver flow. Grace to add rotation API details; Laura to add incident gating / retention notes to playbook.
4) Compliance: ensure proxy does not persist assertions; Okta confirmed group claims option.
5) Ops: add /health and /metrics requirement; quarterly emergency path test.

Attachments: delegated-admin-playbook.docx (draft), scim_group_map_v1.csv (Marcus comments pending), saml_authn_proxy_flow.png

I scheduled a 30m design-review on Friday 2024-05-17 10:00 PT and invited DataHub SREs. Please update the playbook before then — I'm happy to present.
